full_judgment:
2. Upon FIR lodged by one Suharabuddin @ Hiru about occurrence as to murder of his elder sister Anisa Khatun by unknown miscreants in her late husband's house in village Nahali PS Mirzapur District Tangail in the night following 13-5-2005, Mirzapur PS Case No. 6 dated 15-5-2005 was started. Subsequently, on conclusion of investigation charge sheet under sections 460/302/34, Penal Code was submitted against accused 1. SM Mozammel Haque Talukder Shahajan Talukder @ Shahajan 2. Nazemuddin @ Nazim Member 3. Nazrul Islam 4. Amjad Hossain @ Anju Mia 5. Md Badsha Mea. During investigation accused Nazrul Islam made inculpatory confessional statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure involving himself and other above named accused in the commission of the offence as to murder of Anisa Khatun. 

 8. Learned Advocate refers to CC of order No. 38 dated 28-11-2006 and shows that vide said order Druta Bichar Tribunal extended for last 15 working days for conclusion of trial and disposal of the case with observation that 120 working days already expired meanwhile. But learned Advocate shows from CC of order No. 54 dated 16-4-2007 wherein the learned Druta Bichar Tribunal wrongly observed that there were still 13 working days for conclusion of the trial and with such wrong observation rejected the prayer of the accused for return of the case record to original Court for disposal where from it was transferred to Druta Bichar Tribunal. Learned Advocate earnestly argues that Druta Bichar Tribunal cannot withhold the case record with it for conclusion of trial of the case as period of 135 working days already expired as evident from order No. 38 dated 28-11-2006. He accordingly, contends that impugned order dated 16-4-2007 must be set aside and the case record must be directed to be returned back to the original Court due to expiry of the period of 135 working days for conclusion of trial by Druta Bichar Tribunal as per provisions of Druta Bichar Ain as discussed above. Learned Advocate refers to an unreported decision dated 14-3-2007 in Criminal Revision No. 785 of 2007 in the case of Kamrul Islam and others vs State by a Division Bench presided over by Mr Justice Sharifuddin Chaklader. 

 17. In above regard learned Assistant Attorney-General refers to the decision in the case of Al-Amin and 5 others vs State reported in 51 DLR 154, wherein it was held while making interpretation of section 22, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 1995 that on reading of the Provisions contained in section 22 of the Ain it is manifest that there is no penal provision. In the absence of any penal provisions the conclusion of the trial within 90 days cannot be treated as mandatory rather the same is mere directory. 

 18. Learned Assistant Attorney-General also refers to the decision in the case of Delwar Hossain vs State reported in 2006 BLD (AD) 109 wherein it was held that although section 20 of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 1995 laid down a period of 90 days for conclusion of trial with a further Provision in section 20(3) of the Ain to conclude the trial within an extended period of thirty more days, the Act does not provide for any consequence for failure of the trial Court to conclude the trial within one hundred and twenty days. Said Provision appears to be not mandatory rather directory. 

 20. We have heard both sides as above in detail. We have also perused the decisions reported in 55 DLR 636, 56 DLR 31, perused unreported decision dated 14-3-2007 in Criminal Revision No. 785 of 2007 in the case of Kamrul Islam and others vs State by Division Bench presided over by Mr Justice Sharifuddin Chaklader as cited on behalf of accused-appellants. We have also perused decisions reported in 51 DIR 154 and 2006 BLD (AD) 109 cited by learned Assistant Attorney-General. 

 26. In the case of Lakhman Sastri vs State of Bihar reported m AIR 1967 Pat 160 it was observed that the time clause will not be considered to be mandatory unless its non-observance will result in the object of the provision being frustrated. 

 32. In such regard we may took at the provisions of section 10(5) wherein it has been stated that the returned back case from Tribunal will get top priority in the mother Court but if there be any pending hearing of any case in the mother Court at the moment of receipt of the returned back case, the hearing of said pending case has to be concluded first and thereafter the hearing of the returned back case will commence and it will continue without any break till conclusion of the trial. From above it is obvious that the mother Court cannot take up the hearing of the returned back case promptly at once for speedy disposal soon after receipt of the same from Tribunal as stated in the provisions of section 10(5) itself. But in the Tribunal there is no such bar and it can go with trial and disposal of the case in its usual manner even after expiry of the specified time of 135 working days. We find spirit of speedy trial and disposal of the case can be maintained more properly and appropriately in the Tribunal than in the mother Court as noticed above. 

 37. In above regard we are to be guided by the observation in the decision of the case of Delwar Hossain vs State reported in 2006 BLD (AD) 109 wherein it was held, that although section 20 of the Ain (Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 1995) laid down a period of 90 days for conclusion of trial with further provision in section 20(3) to conclude the trial within an extended period of thirty more days, the Act does not provide for any consequence for failure of the trial Court to conclude the trial within one hundred twenty days. This provision is not mandatory rather directory. 

 44. Order as to stay of the further proceeding of the Druta Bichar Case No. 8 of 2006 issued earlier by this Division be recalled. Druta Bichar Tribunal No. 2 Dhaka is to proceed with the hearing and trial of above Druta Bichar case with due notice to both sides through engaged Advocates and to fix up convenient date for argument of the case after recording statements under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the accused as prosecution evidence was already closed and concluded as evident from order dated 16-4-2007. 

 51. From the plain reading of the above provision we find that the law only says that if the case cannot be disposed of within the time fixed by the law the Tribunal will send back the case to the original Court from where it was transferred to the Tribunal by informing the Supreme Court and the Government in writing. In that law we do not find any such phrases and words as to give an impression that the said provision is a mandatory one as it is found in some other provisions of law. For example, section 96(3)(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act made it compulsory that while filing the case of pre-emption the entire amount of consideration money together with compensation must be accompanied with the application for pre-emption otherwise the application is not competent and not maintain-able. This provision is a mandatory one as the non-compliance of the law results in a fatal consequence. Let us now see the construction of that law. Section 96(3)(a) runs thus: 

 "Application made under sub-section 1 shall be dismissed unless the applicant or applicants at the time of making it, deposit in the Court the amount of the consideration money or the value of the transferred holding or portion or share of the holding as stated in the notice under section 89 or in the deed of transfer, as the case may be together with compensation at the rate of per centum of such amount."
